finding.title: OS Command Injection
finding.assumptions: m_name is derived from user input or another untrusted source and is used in a way that could be interpreted by a shell.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Attempted to determine whether the use of std::ofstream::open could trigger shell command execution. Verified that std::ofstream::open directly calls the underlying OS open(2) system call (or equivalent) and does not invoke a shell or interpret metacharacters in the file name. Therefore, even though m_name may contain characters such as spaces, quotes, or shell metacharacters, they are treated as literal characters in the file path rather than as shell syntax, and no OS command injection can occur.

finding.title: Improper Neutralization of Special Elements used in an OS Command ('OS Command Injection')
finding.trigger: If m_name contains special characters that could be used in an OS command
finding.assumptions: m_name is derived from user input or another untrusted source and is used in a way that could be interpreted by a shell.

parsed.refutation_attempt:
Verified that the sink m_os->open() uses std::ofstream::open, which opens a file directly via the C++ standard library and does not invoke a shell or any command interpreter. No path from m_name to system(), exec, or popen is present. Even if m_name contains characters such as spaces, semicolons, or newlines, they are treated as literal parts of the file path, not as command separators. Therefore, OS Command Injection is not possible.

No additional checks or neutralizations are needed because the operation is inherently safe against command injection.

finding.title: Improper Control of Generation of Code ('Code Injection')
finding.trigger: If m_name contains characters that could be used to inject code
finding.assumptions: m_name is derived from user input or another untrusted source and is used in a way that could be interpreted by a shell.

parsed.refutation_attempt: Checked the use of m_os->open: it calls std::ofstream::open which opens a file directly with the provided path, without invoking any shell or command interpreter. The filename is constructed solely from m_name and static suffixes, and the file stream does not interpret shell metacharacters. Thus the reported code injection cannot occur.
